generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a stemless clump of thick, fleshy, grey-green leaves 30 to 50 cm long (Britton and Millspaugh 1920: 3 dm to 6 dm; a pup's first leaves are far shorter, so the length is not checked over every leaf) and 6 to 7 cm wide at the base, triangular in section, with small soft teeth along the margins. Its flowering follows Britton (1918) and Britton and Millspaugh (1920): a stout scape about 0.8 m to 1.2 m high ends in a dense raceme 10 cm to 30 cm long (stalk_height 0.9, stalk_head 0.2, 40 flowers) of yellow flowers about 2.5 cm long, hanging on short pedicels (flower_angle 150, nodding). Britton (1918) calls the plant stoloniferous, and garden plants crowd with offsets: a crown that flowers may also send out a pup that year, and pups send out up to two of their own (bloom_pup 1, pup_pups 2), so the clump spreads outward. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge, with the flowering spike: a quarter metre in its third year, about 0.8 m once it flowers. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs, made paler and greyer to match Britton's (1918) 'pale glaucous-green' leaves: grey-green leaves with pale teeth, yellow flowers. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): six yellow tepals joined in a tube, six stamens and a superior pistil of three carpels, from the characters of its own and Asphodelaceae's by the rules at the flowering plants. The tepals close into a tube (cup 80, curl 15), the genus's near-cylindric perianth with spreading tips (Britton 1918). Teeth about 1.2 cm apart, within Britton's (1918) 1.3 cm or less.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Flora of North America's account of the species, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read: tepals 6, prominently 3-veined, connate basally for half their length; stamens 6, slightly unequal, included to slightly exserted. The Finnish Biodiversity Information Facility calls the perianth tubular, up to 3 cm long (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Britton and Millspaugh (1920): scape 8 dm to 12 dm high, above a nearly stemless rosette, so a flowering plant stands about that tall.

generator.params.stalk_height.note: Britton (1918), Flora of Bermuda, under Aloe vera: scape stout, 0.6 m to 1.1 m high (2 to 3.5 feet; Britton and Millspaugh 1920 give 8 dm to 12 dm), above a nearly stemless, stoloniferous rosette. Converted from feet; in our own words.

generator.params.stalk_head.note: Britton (1918): raceme dense, 10 cm to 30 cm long (4 to 12 inches), a fifth of a 0.9 m stalk. The count of 40 flowers is ours, for a dense raceme.

generator.params.flower_angle.note: Britton (1918), for the genus Aloe: flowers nodding in racemes, the perianth near cylindric with its tips somewhat spreading; for Aloe vera, flowers yellow, about 2.5 cm long, on pedicels shorter than their bracts. 150 degrees hangs each flower down from the stalk.

generator.params.bloom_pup.note: Britton (1918) calls Aloe vera stoloniferous: offsets crowd round the rosette whether or not it flowers, so a flowering crown may also send out a pup (bloom_pup 1), and pups send out up to two of their own (pup_pups 2, ours), so the clump spreads outward.
